title: Integrated fault detection and supervisory compensation for hydronic radiator faults in district-heated buildings
description: Code, trained detectors and simulation inputs accompanying the article "Integrated fault detection and supervisory compensation for hydronic radiator faults in district-heated buildings", published in Results in Engineering (2026), doi:10.1016/j.rineng.2026.113471. Three unsupervised anomaly detectors, trained only on a fault-free heating season, run inside the EnergyPlus solver through the Python API. A signature-based ladder classifies the detected anomaly as a stuck-closed valve, a zone-level over-delivery setpoint bias, or a system-level supply-temperature setpoint bias, and a supervisory controller adjusts the district-heating supply setpoint accordingly within the same simulation. The repository covers detector training, the in-the-loop runtime, the severity and compensation-parameter sweeps, the compound-fault stress tests, and the analysis that produces the reported tables.
